opener: A labour hutment is the room-based member of the SAMAN worker housing range: a linear block of individual sleeping rooms, each with its own personnel door, aluminium sliding window, fans and a small distribution board. Crews get lockable rooms rather than one shared hall, which suits mixed gangs and longer postings. The block is a welded or bolted MS structure with an insulated corrugated exterior, built in six sizes between 60x24 ft G+1 and 120x24 ft G+2 that house 58 to 216 workers. Every size is priced ex-factory on a single square-foot rate.
descriptionHtml:
The Labour Hutment: Rooms, Not Halls

A hutment block trades a little capacity for a lot of order. Each floor is divided into separate sleeping rooms along a passage, each room having a lockable door, sliding aluminium window, fan points and its own small board. Workers keep belongings behind a lock, gangs keep to their own rooms, and supervisors stop refereeing the disputes open halls generate.

Where Rooms Beat Halls

Long postings are the hutment's home ground. When a crew stays on site season after season, not week after week, privacy stops being a luxury and becomes the reason workers stay. Several principal contractors now write room-based accommodation into subcontract audit standards, and the hutment is the building that passes those audits without argument.

Six Hutment Sizes

SizeBuilt areaWorkers (planning)Price ex-GST
60x24 ft G+12,880 sq ft58 to 72Rs 19,82,880
90x24 ft G+14,320 sq ft86 to 108Rs 29,74,320
90x24 ft G+26,480 sq ft129 to 162Rs 44,61,480
120x24 ft G+15,760 sq ft115 to 144Rs 39,65,760
118x30 ft G+17,080 sq ft142 to 177Rs 48,74,580
120x24 ft G+28,640 sq ft173 to 216Rs 59,48,640

Rooms repeat identically on every floor, so a bigger block means more rooms, never different rooms.

Block Construction

The structure is MS framing, welded or bolted to suit the site, behind an insulated corrugated skin. Floors are board on steel joists, and services run room by room so a fault in one room never darkens the block. The passage carries its own night circuit, and the stair tower on the three-floor block includes the luggage winch point moving day demands. Full component detail sits in the Specifications tab.

Allocation Is the Hidden Feature

Rooms turn accommodation management into a paper exercise. Gangs, trades and shifts are separated door by door; day and night shifts separate by floor without anyone policing a stair. Chargehands take the end rooms, the caretaker sits beside the entrance, and the same keys go to the same gangs season after season.

Hutment Pricing

Rs 688.50 per square foot ex-GST, flat across the ladder, a small premium over the open hall that buys the partitions, doors and per-room services. The rate runs slightly above the open-hall shed building for the same area with a lower bed count per floor; that is the deliberate trade. Crews that relocate should weigh the demountable camp block instead, and the colony range overview sets all three side by side.

Ordering and Delivery

Send headcount and posting length with the enquiry; the quotation returns inside 48 hours with a room schedule and passage plan drawn for the size you pick. Dispatch trails approval by 7 to 21 working days, with the standard warranty cover of 5 years structural, 1 year finishing.

Why the Hutment Comes From SAMAN

Room modules are fabricated, not improvised, so door swings, window heights and board positions are identical in room forty and room four. Manufacturer pricing keeps the room premium honest, and our two-facility footprint serves postings in any state.

Labour Hutment FAQs

How many workers per room?

Standard rooms take four to eight depending on bunk layout; the room schedule in your quotation shows the exact fit.

Can couples or staff be housed?

End rooms are routinely allocated to couples employed on site and to supervisory staff.

Do rooms have power points?

Each room carries lighting, fan points and sockets on its own small board.

What happens when a room's electrics fault?

Only that room is affected; per-room services isolate faults by design.

Is the block relocatable?

It moves once if it must, but repeated moves are the camp block's job, not the hutment's.
